_readme: This is the one file to edit. Change any text below, save, then commit (see README).
Lines starting with EDIT: are placeholders that still need real info from the team.
robot.front: which way the robot faces at the start. "auto" points the intake at the viewer; or use +x, -x, +z, -z.
match: words that appear in Onshape sub-assembly or part names. Parts that match nothing go to Frame & Structure.
camera (optional, per subsystem): { "azimuth": degrees around, "elevation": degrees above the floor, "zoom": 1 = default, 1.3 = closer }.
After changing match words, run: npm run model

subsystems.name: Swerve Drive
subsystems.summary: EDIT: Four independently steered modules let us drive in any direction while rotating.
talkingPoints: EDIT: Field-oriented control means the driver pushes the stick toward a spot on the field and the robot goes there, no matter which way it faces.
EDIT: Inverted MK4i modules keep motors low and protected inside the frame.
EDIT: Absolute encoders remember each wheel's angle, so we never re-zero between matches.

subsystems.name: Roller Bar Intake
subsystems.summary: EDIT: A full-width roller bar that pulls game pieces off the floor on contact.
talkingPoints: EDIT: Touch it, own it: compliant rubber rollers grab pieces even at awkward angles.
EDIT: Two roller stages hand pieces straight into the hopper with no stops.
EDIT: Built to survive hits from defense: the bar folds back instead of bending.

subsystems.name: Hopper & Indexer
subsystems.summary: EDIT: Stores game pieces and lines them up for the turrets one at a time.
talkingPoints: EDIT: Mecanum rollers push pieces sideways and forward at once, so they never jam in the corners.
EDIT: The indexer splits the stream evenly between both turrets.
EDIT: Polycarb side walls let the drive team see how full we are.

subsystems.name: Twin Turrets
subsystems.summary: EDIT: Two independently aiming turrets that score from anywhere while we drive.
talkingPoints: EDIT: Each turret tracks the target on its own, so the driver can focus on driving.
EDIT: Heavy brass flywheels keep their speed between shots for consistent range.
EDIT: The adjustable hood changes the shot angle based on distance from the goal.

subsystems.name: Electrical & Controls
subsystems.summary: EDIT: Clean, serviceable wiring with vision, power and status all in easy reach.
talkingPoints: EDIT: Two Limelight cameras give the turrets their aim and keep track of our position on the field.
EDIT: Every wire is labeled and the brain pan opens for fast pit repairs.
EDIT: The main breaker and battery plug sit on the outside for quick swaps between matches.

subsystems.name: Frame & Structure
subsystems.summary: EDIT: A rigid aluminum chassis and bumpers that tie every mechanism together.
talkingPoints: EDIT: Riveted gussets keep the frame square after hard hits.
EDIT: Bumpers attach with hinges and pins so we can swap colors in under a minute.
EDIT: Designed in Onshape so everyone on the team can edit the same model.
